# occ -- one row per occupation.
#
# Replaces balance_occupation_slots_effects.txt, which spelled out 32,730 numbered
# slots so that a row could be addressed without an array index. A global
# variable map is keyed by a runtime number, so the index the language was
# missing is available after all: the row counter is the key and each column is
# its own map. The bucket walk, the slot ceiling and the generated file all go.
#
# Read from the save under `variables.map_data`, one container per column:
#
#     map_data={ { name="occ_loc"
#                  list={ { key={ type=value identity=<row * 100000> }
#                           value={ ... } } ... } } }
#
# Keys are the row number and come back in no particular order -- sort by key.
# Numbers carry the usual x100000 scale. Rows are paired across columns by key,
# so column A's key 7 and column B's key 7 are the same row.
#
# Columns (3), each a map of its own:
#     loc      <- scope:target
#     by       <- root
#     d        <- current_date
#
# global_var:occ_count is still the row count and still the last key written.

occ_increment_and_log = {
	if = {
		limit = { NOT = { has_global_variable = occ_count } }
		set_global_variable = { name = occ_count value = 0 }
	}
	change_global_variable = { name = occ_count add = 1 }

	add_to_global_variable_map = { name = occ_loc key = global_var:occ_count value = scope:target }
	add_to_global_variable_map = { name = occ_by key = global_var:occ_count value = root }
	add_to_global_variable_map = { name = occ_d key = global_var:occ_count value = current_date }
}
